red_audit_note: The orchestrator's independent re-run of ddad1bf5 must show `bash scripts/tests/test_check_board_currency.sh` rc=1 with exactly 58 PASS and 15 FAIL. Measured on byte-identical content immediately before the commit. The 15 FAILs partition as: 5 from Arm 18 (landed slice with no ladder sha — 1 recurrence + 1 slice-name + 3 anti-vacuity lines that fire pre-fix only because the fixture's PASSING cross-read summary line contains the words `remaining_ladder`), 1 from Arm 19, 3 from Arm 20 (missing STALE prefix / missing type diagnostic / raw traceback present), 3 from Arm 21, 2 from Arm 22b and 2 from Arm 22c. NO DEVIATION: the arms commit touches only scripts/tests/test_check_board_currency.sh; the fix commit touches only scripts/check-board-currency.sh and scripts/preflight.sh.

A.statement: `sha = (by_slice.get(key) or {}).get("sha")` followed by `if sha and sha not in status:` made check (c) — the LOAD-BEARING half of the TC-133 cross-read — a silent NO-OP for any slice listed in `landed` whose `ladder` entry is missing or carries no `sha`. The gate then certified the hand-written row on the strength of check (b), the marker regex the file's own comment calls the fragile half. That is exactly the state-file incompleteness this step was added to catch.
A.real_state_measurement: REQUIRED BY THE BRIEF AND PERFORMED BEFORE CHOOSING THE FIX. Every one of the 14 ids in `landed` in dev/plans/release-state-0.8.20.json — 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 21, 22, 23, 25, 30, 31, 32, 33, 39 — has a `ladder` entry AND a non-null, non-empty string `sha` (403eb254, 1f8ed8bf, 3cfb3cda, a2022957, 841c307b, 83b1c818, 9b3ed0e3, 77be504b, 572475f2, 30102ecd, d0287620, 31d33293, f02dc5b4, 91db34d8). ZERO landed slices lack one, so a hard fail cannot redden the live gate. Confirmed end-to-end: `bash scripts/check-board-currency.sh` reports `14 landed slice(s) reconciled` and exits 0. The STOP condition was therefore not triggered.
A.fix: The landed-slice loop now resolves the ladder entry FIRST and hard-fails with a specific reason when it is absent, when it carries no `sha` key, or when `sha` is not a non-empty string; check (c) then consumes that resolved value instead of re-deriving it through the `or {}` construct. The non-empty-STRING requirement is deliberate: `sha` is used as `sha not in status`, where a non-string is either a TypeError or a silently wrong answer.

B.statement: Leg 3 validated KEY PRESENCE but not TYPE. A state file whose `landed`/`ladder`/`remaining_ladder` had the wrong type sailed past validation and detonated in a later loop as an UNPREFIXED Python traceback. The standalone checker exits non-zero, but `preflight.sh --landing` promoted only `STALE*` lines to HARD and turned every other line into INFO — so the cross-read's failure was DOWNGRADED and the tree was CERTIFIED FOR LANDING. Measured pre-fix: `preflight.sh --landing` rc=0 on that tree.
B.fix_part_1_type_validation: `landed`, `ladder` and `remaining_ladder` must each be a JSON array, and `ladder` must be an array of OBJECTS. Diagnostics are raised into the existing handler, which emits them with the `STALE` prefix preflight promotes to HARD. The `ladder`-of-objects half is not cosmetic: the map builder guarded itself with `isinstance(entry, dict)`, so `"ladder": [5, 40]` silently DROPPED every entry, the map came out EMPTY, and check (c) then evaporated via finding A's construct — two independent fail-opens composing into one green with rc=0, no exception and no diagnostic (Arm 21). That guard has been removed now that the type is validated.

determination.question: [DETERMINE] the correct locus for closing the GENERAL fail-open — a future unexpected exception anywhere in the cross-read must surface as a hard failure during landing, never as an unprefixed traceback downgraded to INFO.
determination.chosen: (ii) harden scripts/preflight.sh §7 so a NON-ZERO EXIT from check-board-currency.sh is HARD regardless of what it printed.
determination.why_rejected_measured: A Python-level catch can only cover what is raised INSIDE that Python. MEASURED, not asserted, against the shipped script: `bash scripts/check-board-currency.sh --tip nosuchref` exits 2 printing `check-board-currency: --tip nosuchref does not resolve to a commit`, and `bash scripts/check-board-currency.sh --bogus` exits 2 printing `check-board-currency: unknown arg --bogus` — both with ZERO `STALE` lines, i.e. both fully downgraded to INFO by the old §7. The script also runs under `set -euo pipefail` after sourcing scripts/lib/board-closed.sh, so a missing/broken lib, a failing `git log`, or any future bash-level check aborts it the same way. Option (i) closes the INSTANCE codex demonstrated, not the CLASS codex named.
determination.why_chosen: It is the more robust invariant AND, contrary to the brief's framing, the SMALLER blast radius of the two: the guard is additive and can only fire on a run that is ALREADY non-zero, so it cannot turn a green land red (pinned by Arm 22d). It is also not a new idiom — preflight §8 (ledger-integrity), §9 (governed-surface-pin), §10 (c1-conformance) and §11 (transcript-hygiene) ALL already carry exactly this anti-fail-open guard, with near-identical wording. §7 was the ONE landing sub-gate missing it, because it predates the idiom; this REMOVES AN ASYMMETRY rather than inventing an invariant. CI needed nothing: the always-on board-currency job fails on any non-zero exit already — preflight was the only downgrader.

determination.deliberate_non_fix: The UnicodeDecodeError in fixture W is left UNHANDLED on purpose and is documented as such in the test. Its subject is not that exception; it is the invariant that ANY unanticipated failure hard-blocks a land on the strength of the exit code alone. Giving it a bespoke handler would delete the arm, leave the invariant untested for the next unanticipated exception, and would be widening beyond the two findings codex raised.
